- **MOON V4 V1 (2026-11-03, Moon Caves v4, milestone V1: the skeleton; branch `g-moon-v4`, NOT PUSHED; hidden behind `MC_V4` (dev flag only), v3 untouched; the owner on V0's pictures: "it is good. build."):** `mc4Build(side, moon)` builds the V0 plan as plain geometry: the rock mass minus rooms (each room of caves 1 to K-1 a box of its footprint, floor on the cave's floor, roof where the plan put it; a tall hall also cuts the floors of the caves above it, which keep a one-way bridge over it), a flat throat (128 px high, never under 112) through the plug between neighbouring rooms (none across a pole in a SPLIT or FAN cave), each team's home (the strip) with v3's lift, steps, pads and hop-tops, the surface lap (v3's hop-tops; no stair-holes yet), the furnace as v3 (cracks, hot floor, stones: the bays are plain), the shell and strips as v3's numbers copied into `MC4_B` (never read from `MC_GEN`). The ROOM GRAPH (`g.g4`: a node for the surface, the furnace, each home of each cave, each room, each foot of a hall; edges lat / lift / drop) has a NEXT-HOP TABLE per team (a team never routes through the other's home); the CPU's router reads it through `mc4Route`, `mc4PathCost` and `mc4Walk` (the three one-line hooks in `mcRoute`, `mcPathCost`, `mcRouteSteer`). `MC4.pick` (dev override `bfsi:mc4moon` 1 to 16, else a draw never the last moon of that size; until V9 a moon number is the preview mapping seed = side x 10000 + 1 + moon). Stage hooks 1-5: `mooncaves4` row in `STAGES`, `stageOpen` first test, `buildMoonCaves`, `mcState` (`v`, `moon`, `g4`). Diff outside the marked block: 3 router one-liners, `buildMoonCaves`, `mcState`, the `STAGES` row, `stageOpen` (+ the V4 block's header comment). The planner is text-identical to V0's fix commit (`0df36fb`) except one comment and one console line, so every plan hash is unchanged. **Differs from the spec, and why:** (1) `mcLayer` itself is unchanged (a cave is still found by radius; v4's caves sit at the same radii), the room lookup is `mc4NodeAt` (cave by radius, then the room of that cave by angle; between two rooms the nearer), used by the router and the cost; (2) a hall's drop: the one-way bridge cannot be dropped through by a CPU (Down with a Jump came out of the CPU's hands as a drop and then a jump back up, and at the bridge's edge the rock beside it stepped the body back onto the bridge), so the CPU walks to the middle of the bridge and lets itself through (`mc4Walk`: `dropping`, as other AI code does); a person still drops with Down; (3) in the home's shaft a CPU whose next hop is sideways comes down over the side it goes on to (straight down the middle it fell on through the next band's opening: the homes are one straight column through every depth, as in v3), and coming down through a hall's air it aims straight down (the gap hop spent its other jump and it went back up onto the bridge); (4) the screen check's lines (below) cannot all be met by a skeleton of plain boxes: recorded, not tuned. **Checks (scratchpad `moon-v4/v1/`, all short throwaway scripts, none committed):** syntax; boot (`ffa bad positions 0 teams bad positions 0 errors none`); CRLF (116,744 lines, 0 bare LF). **Geometry, all 14 sizes x 16 moons = 224 builds:** 0 faults in 6,000 sample points per moon (every point of a cave's air band is rock or exactly one space, none both), every wall between two spaces at least 100 px (min 100.0), every throat at least 112 px, every piece valid, every piece and zone has its mirror partner (S3), mean 173 pieces and 47 nodes a moon. **S1** (switch off, origin/ii-dlc `a2a7797`, same session): `mcGeoOut` hash, piece hash and a fingerprint of the whole `mcGen` output equal at 2, 4, 7, 10 and 15 a side (n 219, 219, 303, 356, 570 pieces), and a 1,800-frame CPU match on v3 plays on both, 0 errors; the stage is out of every list with the switch off and in the Teams list only with it on (never in FFA). **S2** v4 boots and a 60-second CPU match plays at 4 a side (moons 1, 3, 9) and 10 a side (moons 7, 12), 0 errors, 0 bad positions; plan sweep 14 sizes x 200 seeds: 99.79% within 8 tries (6 fallbacks of 2,800; worst size 14 a side 98.0%; the planner is untouched). **S4:** every room is reachable in the graph from both homes and from the surface (0 misses in 224 moons); the per-team tables miss only the rooms of the other team's half of a SPLIT or FAN cave (2,952 room-ends in 224 moons, 0 elsewhere: by design, "the teams cannot meet in them"); scripted CPU walks (a CPU from its home pad to a still foe set in a room, fresh page each): 4 a side all 16 moons 64 of 64 targets (rooms, halls' feet and the furnace), 10 a side 8 moons 44 of 44; CPU-only matches: 3 minutes at 4 a side 0 stuck windows (longest still 207 frames = 3.5 s), 2 minutes at 10 a side (the 90 s run budget) 0 stuck windows (longest 213 frames), KOs 1 and 1 (space), v3's baseline 137 s at 4 a side: longest still 176 frames. **S5 (before V8b):** two builds of the same moon in one process, and in a fresh page, give the same plan hash and piece hash and identical next-hop tables (7 moons). **Screen check on the real geometry (`screens.mjs`; - **MOON V4 V1 FIX (2026-11-03, after the V1 checker; branch `g-moon-v4`, NOT PUSHED):** (1) SHOULD-FIX, hall caps: in `mc4Build` the roof of a hall's top-cave foot is now `min(max(rc + hh, tops[top] + 128), airTop(top))`, so the air over the one-way bridge is never under a throat's height (128 px). Before: 127 of 1,575 top-of-hall feet were under 112 px (82 under 90) and the checker's flood fill at body half-size 48 left 48 of 224 moons with a foot or room unreachable (136 nodes). After: the lowest top foot in the 224 moons is 128 px (0 under 112, 0 under 104, 0 under 90), and the same flood fill (8 px cells, a square body, nodes' floor spots, 224 moons) at half-size 24 AND 48 has 0 bad nodes in all 224 moons. THE PLANNER IS NOT TOUCHED: a one-line geometry change in mc4Build, so the plan hashes are UNCHANGED (the clamp only raises a roof the plan left in the first 128 px; the planner's own rule to reject such a hall was not needed). The room's recorded height (own.h) only grows, so a throat can only keep its 128 px. (2) NOTE, screen-check lines: nothing to change in the game; the director writes down before V2 how the district-twin line (5% taken from 6.3 as its own number, not 2 x the 1% reading) and the two 'at least' lines are derived. Left as built; V3 (the Crawl) and the planner's plug minimum must agree (plug rock at 112 or more, or the plug minimum becomes 100): DECIDE AT V3. (5) NOTE, ii-dlc: merged local ii-dlc (6f291d3: camera KO line, Pencil's van; origin/ii-dlc still a2a7797) into the branch as 275bffa, both ledger rows kept; they do not touch mcGen. (6) NOTE, the pictures are a skeleton's: caves differ only in colour and room size; V2 on moves the screen-check numbers. - **2026-11-03, BOW TELEPORT KEEPS SPEED (the owner: "is this a bug: when I use teleport, it cancels my momentum, allowing me to carry stocks for very long."; he chose exactly two changes; branch `g-bow-tp`, NOT PUSHED):** It was not a bug but it was a loophole: the Teleport zeroed her speed at both ends (`startTeleport`, `teleportStep`, `teleportArrive`), held her still for `TP.hang` (6 frames) where she appeared, made her untouchable while she faded, and gave itself back when she was HIT (`_tpUsed` reset on `hitstun`), so a launched Bow could teleport, stop dead, be hit again and teleport again. CHANGE 1, SHE KEEPS HER SPEED: if she was hit this airtime (`_tpLaunch`, set while `hitstun > 0` and cleared on a floor, on a KO and on a new stock) and moves `TP.keep` = 2.5 px a frame or more on the press, that speed (vx, vy, read on the press frame after that frame's air control) is remembered on the `_tp` object and given back the frame she appears, and the 6-frame hang is skipped for it (the simplest way to really keep it: the hang would otherwise hold her still with no gravity). The bar is low on purpose: hits here are slow (a side launch is 4-8 px a frame and nothing slows it in the air). A jump, a drift or a use on the stage (no hit this airtime) is exactly as before: zeroed, then the hang. Distance (240), the fade (8 frames), invulnerability while fading, CTF/carrier/copy scaling, the pop damage and the CPU's reads are untouched. CHANGE 2, A HIT NO LONGER GIVES IT BACK: the `_tpUsed` reset is now on landing only (and still on a KO and a new stock; the cancel in `teleportStep`, where a freeze or sneeze ended the fade before she went anywhere, still refunds it). Nothing was added to the wire: the host does the move, a guest sees her position (`x`, `y`, `vx`, `vy`, `_tpUsed`, `_tp`, `_tpHang` are already in the snapshot). Text: Bow's move card (Teleport) and kit line say she keeps her speed after a hit and gets the move back only on landing; one line on the What's new card. PROOF (jsdom, Goiky Field: floor ends at x 922, world 1024, right KO line 1304 = 382 past the ledge; Bow hit off the right ledge, `applyHit` with her at 100% and 150%, free after 26 frames of hitstun at x 1008-1072 moving 4.4-7 px a frame; she presses Teleport the first free frame; scripts in the session scratchpad `bowtp/`, before = ii-dlc): TOWARD THE STAGE (left): before, she appears 240 px back at speed 0 and lives, on the floor, every time (A: 100%, vx 7: appears at x 832, speed 0, lives; B: 150%, vx 7: 838, lives; D: 100%, vx 4.4: 768, lives); after, she appears at the same spot (839, 844, 772) with her speed (6.1, 6.1, 3.4 px a frame away from the stage after that frame's left key) and, if the player lets go, drifts off the ledge and is KO'd on frame 76, 75 (A, B) or lives (D, the slow one: 3.4 px a frame is slowed to a stop and lands); if the player steers back (holds left while she is moving right) she lives in all three, so the move is still a recovery, no longer a free stop. UP / NO AIM (she is past the world's edge, so the trip is brought just inside, x about 1000): before she appears at speed 0 and is KO'd falling on frame 93-94; after she keeps (7, 2.1) and is carried to the side KO line, 381 px past the ledge, KO'd on frame 81-85. (Up + C is Chair Slam, so 'up' is the neutral aim.) GENTLE USES unchanged: drift of 2 px a frame, no hit (appears 240 px away at speed 0, lives, same as before), standing on the stage (no change), a jump's rise with no hit (no change). A HIT AFTER TELEPORTING: hit in the air after appearing, 30 frames later (cooldown cleared): before, the move was back (a second press started a fade); after it is still spent (the press only puffs) and returns when she lands (36 frames later); a freeze that cancels the fade still refunds it; a KO clears `_tpUsed` and `_tpLaunch`. CPU: Bow in three Expert CPU free-for-alls (Bow/Toothpaste/Firey/Bomby, Bow/Pen/Lifering/Tea Kettle, Bow/Leafy/Rocky/Needle, 2,400 frames each): errors none, bad positions 0; she teleported 4, 2 and 1 times (before 1, 2, 1) and 5 of the 7 kept a launch; she still lives in the same range of stocks. ONLINE (in-process host + guest, no relay): Bow hit out, teleports, same path on both screens: the guest equals the host 3 frames earlier to within 0.5 px over all 134 frames, the teleport included, final position the same. Syntax, boot (ffa and teams, bad positions 0, errors none), CRLF intact. BALANCE NOTE: this nerfs a defensive recovery the owner called too strong; the change is mild where the launch is slow (a light hit she can steer out of) and sharp where it is big (a launch toward the blast zone now still kills her unless she steers back at once, and cannot be chained by hits). Her Final Smash, Chair Slam, Snowballs and the CPU's logic were not touched; the CPU still prefers the Teleport as before and its use after a hit now also costs it the move until it lands. Not tuned further: `TP.keep` (2.5) is the one number if the owner wants more or less.

- **MOON CAVES v4 planner stacking (V7, 2026-11-10, Moon Caves v4; branch `g-moon-v4`, NOT PUSHED; a HIDDEN stage behind `MC_V4` (dev flag only), not in the public stage list, no changelog; THE PLAN HASHES CHANGED (allowed until V9): the table moons are regenerated, e.g. 2-1 42f97ea9, 4-1 ab5357a6, 4-10 713c6fcc, 7-4 2524bdf7, 10-7 d8799e66, 10-16 61f8c2f4, 15-3 34546d01):** The owner chose the planner change after V6 missed the interconnection goal. PLANNER (`mc4Sample`, the built fill of each quarter, cave by cave, deepest first): the cave below is finished, so each built room of the cave being laid out is scored by its best common span (px at the lower radius, capped at 720) with a room of the cave below that can take a window (not a foot, not a pole room, not a hall); the fill takes the best of up to six valid draws (the first on a tie), picks the gap after a room (250 to 790 px, a long one costs a little) that stacks the next room best, and when a start would stack under 400 px looks up to 400 px ahead for one that does (the rock skipped is left to the gap filler). Every old rule is kept (kinds and counts, R1, R2, R9, S3 mirror, poles, the share targets); an 800 px look-ahead made one plan (15-12) fail its score and was cut to 400. WINDOWS (`colFor`, the window pass): the upper room's floor hole needs the floor clear (rock, a plank under 48 px, a zone on the floor) but a one-way plank higher up may stand over it (the Lake's shelves, the Garden's pyramid had blocked every column); in a built lower room a column with only furniture in it and nothing hanging to the roof is now a DROP-ONLY window (no steps; same graph edge as a hatch); a full-clear column stays a hatch with plank steps. A hatch or hub now also has its way back UP in the graph (a `climb` edge, as the Warren's; the CPU's climb is still V8a's). PLUG SHAFTS (new, the second pass of the window pass): a plug of 360 px or more between two built rooms of a cave (flat throat) over a room of the next cave gets a 144 px shaft in the throat floor, 100 px clear of both walls, drop-only (the throat is 128 px high: too low to jump out of), up to three to a quarter after the windows; the built plain room beside the plug lets itself down (its drop point is in the throat). `g4.winQ` (quarters with a window or hub) and `g4.plugShafts` added for the checks. MEASURED over the 224 table moons (same script as V6, `moon7/t0-cycles.mjs`, `m1.mjs`, `t6-v5check.mjs`): BEFORE (V6) -> AFTER: cycle rank per moon 14.91 -> 15.84; caves with a cycle 536/1,008 -> 526/1,008 (not better); edge-disjoint routes per room pair 1.50 -> 1.53 (TARGET 2.0 NOT MET); distinct routes per pair 15.69 -> 18.76; pairs with a single route 2,578 of 5,137 (50.2 percent) -> 2,498 of 5,126 (48.7 percent) (TARGET under 35 percent NOT MET); windows 53 -> 154 (15 of them plug shafts), hubs 20 -> 45; quarters with a window or hub (a clear window column used) about 70 -> 198 of 1,568 (TARGET 600 NOT MET); FAN caves with a three-link room 28/251 -> 80/251 (TARGET 53 met). WHY THE REST IS OUT OF REACH (measured, `moon7/d1-d6`): (1) stacking alone changed almost nothing: rooms of neighbouring caves already overlap 240 px in 536 of 1,568 quarters (499 before); the planner's room list is the limit: only 748 of the 1,568 quarters have a plain built room in the upper cave at all (the rest hold natural rooms, poles, halls and feet, none of which can take a floor hole) and the rooms that can take a window in the cave below cover 35 percent of its arc, so even perfect stacking tops out near 620 quarters with a window candidate, before any furniture is counted; (2) the signature rooms are the problem: of the 499 overlapping pairs in V6 only 64 had a clear column; the Lake never (its island and two shelves leave no 144 px band in 1,000 to 1,400 px), the Geode 31 of 147, the Garden 16 of 51, the Attic 5 of 76, the Crawl 12 of 84, and the natural lower rooms almost never (flat and roofless for 144 px); (3) the edge-disjoint number is a directed count and a drop is one way, so it only moves where a hatch (two-way) or a second lateral link exists. NOT DONE: the reserved window column in the plan (the furniture of the five footing rooms would have to be laid out around it, room by room: the Lake needs a new layout), BRAID's second route (every BRAID cave still has the lap's one cycle; BRAID 350 of 350 here). CHECKS (scratchpad `moon7/`, throwaway): 224 table moons build, 0 errors; geometry 0 faults in every class over all 224 (wall, outside, airInRock, throatLow, badPiece, unreach, unreachHome, noLift, zone, mirror, zone mirror), min wall 100; paper flight check of the five footing rooms 156 analyses, 0 problems (the recipes are unchanged; the new openings reuse the V5/V6 hatch geometry, the plug shafts are drop-only); shapes LAP 176/176, SPLIT 231/231, BRAID 350/350, FAN rooms with three links 80/251; S5 double builds equal in one process and in a fresh page (7 moons, the stage still closed with the switch on and off); 1,105 random routes over the next-hop tables, 0 illegal steps (407 down-only, 60 climbs); CPU-through trials 4-1 (Cathedral to Chute), 8-1 (Cathedral to Geode), 6-2 (Geode to Crawl), 2,400 frames: 0 errors, 0 bad positions, longest any CPU stood still 30, 40, 30 frames; 3 CPU free-for-alls of 3,000 frames on Goiky with the moon off: 0 bad positions, 0 errors, `MCAVE.on` 0; ENGINE WALK on a real body (real `step()`, local controller, no key held; `moon7/w1.mjs`): a belt carried it 180 px in 180 frames (about 2 px a frame), an updraft lifted it from the floor to 483 px and held it near 440, a bounce pad (strength 1.9) threw it 291 px up (v3's 296) and it landed on the perch at 240; syncheck 0 failed; boot `ffa bad positions 0 teams bad positions 0 errors none`; guards control bytes 0, bare LF 0, no hidden names in the added lines. The repo's separate kit guard script was not re-run here (no code outside Moon Caves changed). CRLF kept.
- **MOON CAVES v4 V7 (2026-11-10, Moon Caves v4, milestone V7: kind-owned passages, back-wall kits, colour fade; branch `g-moon-v4`, NOT PUSHED; a HIDDEN stage behind `MC_V4` (dev flag only), not in the public stage list, no changelog; v3 and the planner untouched, every plan hash unchanged):** READING OF THE PLAN (v4-spec-r2 section 9 row V7 and section 5; where the text is loose the simplest reading was taken): the passages a kind owns were already in the plan's link types; V7 enforces them in the BUILDER where it makes the climb between caves, and adds the scenery. KIND-OWNED CLIMBS (`mc4Climb`, one helper for the cut-level ladders and the layer-level hatches, hubs and windows): the climb up a 144 px column belongs to the kind of the cave it climbs FROM. SPRINGS have no stairs: a chain of bounce pads (one on the floor under the hole and one on each plank, the planks 200 px apart, v3's strengths 1.3 low and 1.9 normal, a throw reaches about 296 px); UPDRAFTS have a draught only (a column of rising air 90 px wide, no planks); MINES put a belt (30 px) on every step plank, running toward the next plank's end so it brings you to the jump; galleries, columns, flooded, tunnels, the furnace and the surface keep the plank steps (the spec lets only galleries, columns and the surface own stairs; flooded, tunnels and the furnace keep them for lack of a rule, and the planner's room table is not touched). ICE owns ramps only: a WINDOW into an ice cave is a drop with no way back up (the lifts and the ramp rooms are the ways up); a hub's hatch and a room's own ladder (a pit's way out) keep the steps, because a third link or the way out of a pit cannot be dropped. WHAT IS NOT DONE, ON PURPOSE: the homes' lifts keep v3's steps in every kind (they are v3's own ways between caves); the Chimney keeps its plank ledges (an updraft elevator through its bridges was judged too risky for this milestone); the lateral throats keep their sills and slope-mouths. In the 224 table moons (counted per half) the builder laid 104 plank climbs, 22 pad chains, 40 belt climbs and 232 ice drops; no updrafts cave gets a draught climb in the table (their rooms are halls or natural rooms, which are never a window's lower room) so the draught is built and tested only as a zone. SCENERY (v4 moons only: `M.g4`; the v3 moon keeps `MC_LOOK`): `MC4_LOOK` is the spec's palette (galleries warm slate with marble planks, springs purple, columns deep teal with glass planks, updrafts night blue, flooded green-black with mossy rock; the rest as v3). BACK-WALL KITS (`mc4KitBuild`, `mc4KitDraw`, `mc4DrawKit`): built once, lazily, at the first draw from a hash of the cave and the prop's number (no dice: a replay and a guest draw the same), about 3 to 4 props per 1,000 px of a cave's ring, each placed twice and mirrored so the moon is its own mirror image, 130 to 426 props in a moon; no collision; culled by `mcInView`; drawn behind the pieces; none of them is a word. Galleries: arches, banners, lanterns; springs: giant mushrooms, small mushrooms, cyan spore motes; columns: crystal clusters standing and hanging, glints; ice: icicles, frozen falls, snow; updrafts: far floating isles, cloud wisps, rising streaks; mines: timber supports, rails, hanging lamps, ore glints; flooded: half-sunk arches with a waterline, drips, bubbles; tunnels: burrow mouths in the back wall, roots, bones; furnace: pipes, chains, embers, slag pools; the surface: rover tracks in the crust's face and masts with a blinking light. The tint is `mc4DrawMood`: a low-alpha wash over the screen, its colour the cave the camera is in, eased over 150 px (75 px each side of the floor) as the camera crosses a floor, and faded out in the whole-disc watching view; the tunnels get the strongest gloom (alpha 0.18), the others 0.05 to 0.10, the surface none. Hooks outside the block: `mcLookOf`, two lines in `mcDrawDisc`, and the mood call beside the minimap, all guarded by `M.g4`. (2) THE KO SAYS WHO: your KO banner reads "KO'd by Leafy − a stock" (or "You're out! (4) INPUT BUFFER (people only, not CPUs): a jump pressed in the air with no jump left is played if you land within 6 frames, and X pressed while the last move's lag or cooldown was still running is played the moment it ends if that is within 8 frames (before, both were thrown away; smash already worked this way). (9) HIT SOUND: a little pitch variety (about 7% up or down) so a string of jabs is not one note. (10) THE CROWD on the floor line is fainter (0.28, was 0.5) so it is not read as items. - **2026-11-04, DASH ATTACK TELLS (the owner: dash attacks "are very annoying, with no tell. I can think that the cpu is just using a lunge smash, but NOPE, it is an undodgeable (or nearly) dash"; and that Life Ring's "is more fair... I have time to think - oh wait, that isnt coming out, better dodge!"; branch `g-dashtell`):** Measured first. Every special that dashes at a foe fired on the press frame: the dash began at once, 12 to 22 px a frame, so a foe 160 px away was hit 5 to 10 frames after the first sign (Bomb's Collision 7), faster than anyone can react, and nothing a foe did (jump, run away) changed it. Woody's Fraidy Dash, written as a panic dash backwards, in fact dashes FORWARD at 22 px a frame, untouchable, for 12% (the dash code overrides the backwards push), so it was one of them too. Life Ring's whistle (10 frames of wind-up, then a 16 px dash) was the one that already worked: first hit 16 frames after the first sign at 160 px and 18 at 200 px, and a foe who reacts after 12 frames can jump it from 200 px. FIX: one shared helper, `dashTell`, gives every neutral or down special that dashes the same STARTUP Life Ring has (`startWindup`, which the game already draws: the body gathers and glows in its colour), 16 frames long, with a rising whistle, a puff of dust at the feet at the start and more dust every third frame while it gathers. The dash then starts exactly as before: damage, knockback, speed, distance and cooldowns are untouched. A hit on the fighter during the wind-up cancels the dash (as with any startup), so a good player can also stop it by hitting first. Smash dashes (Coiny, Lightning, Leafy, Yin-Yang, Knife, Book, Basketball) already have a 24-frame visible charge before the dash (first sign to first hit 27 to 32 frames at 150 px; the CPU charges them the same way), so they are unchanged. The CPU needs nothing extra: its press is now the wind-up, so it never gets a free instant dash. Covered: Leafy Sprint, Snowball Rage Tackle, Bomb Collision, Balloon Quick Air Release, Pickle dive, Fan charge, Liy Flip the Switch, MeTag cuff, Woody Fraidy Dash (specials), Teddy Bear Front of the Crowd and Bot Gotcha (down specials). Life Ring's own is the benchmark and is not changed. First sign to first hit, foe 160 px away / 200 px away, before then after (frames); wind-up before then after; the foe reacting 12 frames after the press and jumping or running away:
| Dash | Wind-up | First hit at 160 px | First hit at 200 px | Dodgeable with a 12-frame reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bomb Collision | 0 then 16 | 7 then 22 | 10 then 25 | no then yes (jump or run) |
| Snowball Rage Tackle | 0 then 16 | 8 then 23 | 11 then 26 | no then yes |
| Leafy BFDIA Sprint | 0 then 16 | 6 then 21 | 8 then 23 | no then yes (run: hit at 160 only) |
| Teddy Bear Front of the Crowd | 0 then 16 | 8 then 23 | out of range | no then yes |
| Balloon Quick Air Release | 0 then 16 | 6 then 21 | 8 then 23 | no then yes (run: hit at 160 only) |
| Pickle dive | 0 then 16 | 10 then 25 | 13 then 28 | no then running away works; a jump still gets hit at 160 and 200 px (it dives) |
| Liy Flip the Switch | 0 then 16 | 5 then 20 | 7 then 22 | no then yes (run: hit at 160 only) |
| Fan charge | 0 then 16 | 7 then 22 | 10 then 25 | no then yes |
| MeTag cuff | 0 then 16 | 7 then 22 | out of range | no then yes |
| Bot Gotcha | 0 then 16 | 9 then 24 | 13 then 28 | no then yes |

Every dash now reaches the Life Ring window or more at both distances, and a foe beyond the dash's own length (about 190 to 200 px, Leafy's 370) is safe. Bomb Collision in 20 CPU 1v1s against 20 different opponents (same seeds): before, 157 dashes, 29 KOs; after, 207 wind-ups, of which 58 were cancelled by a hit and 149 became dashes, 24 KOs (16 per 100 dashes, 12 per 100 presses; 19 per 100 dashes before); the dash-and-blast hits fell from 256 to 141; Bomb won 17 of the 20 (it won all 20 before). ## Scoreboard

- **2026-11-04, SMASH AUDIT FIXES (the owner, after the Smash Ultimate comparison: "you can fix issues found"; branch `g-smashfix`; balance only, nothing else changed; no picture, no relay, no browser):** Three fixes, each measured before and after with the same scripted scenes (Goiky Field, the attacker at centre stage or 150 px from the left ledge, a foe who stands still; light / mid / heavy foe = Puffball 46, Pen 100, Tree 138; the foe leaving the stage while still in hitstun is a "launched KO"). (1) KILL THROWS, finding: the catalog's "22 back and 22 up throws kill at 100% or less" is a rule on the launch strength alone (it was not measured). Measured on all 109 fighters at centre stage, a MID foe never dies from a back or up throw below 113%: back throws 153 to about 200 (median 181), up throws 113 to 123 (median 123); at the ledge the lowest back throw on a mid foe is 127. Only a LIGHT foe dies early, and only to up throws (64 to 76%, 108 of 109), which the brief allowed ("light foes may die sooner"). Fix: Black Hole's Gravity Boost (up throw, his 'KO throw') was the one throw under the 120% line: its launch ky -13.4 -> -12.2 (damage 6, lag 16, stun 32 unchanged). Lowest KO % before -> after, light / mid / heavy: 64 / 113 / 141 -> 73 / 121 / 149. Every other throw is untouched (none was above Smash's 120 to 160 range, so none is nerfed; none was buffed). Not done, owner's call: the light-foe up throws (64 to 76%); a one-number trim of the shared up throw (GRAB_DEFAULT.u ky -12) would move them, and the mid foe's 121 to 123, by about 3 per 0.5 of ky. (2) JAB KILLS: measured the same way, no plain jab launches a foe out of the stage while still in hitstun before 224% at centre (so none 'kills' in that strict sense); the number that matters (and that the earlier trims used) is the foe leaving the stage at all from centre stage, mid foe, a plain jab: the five already trimmed (Firey, Cake, Match, Magnet, Pencil) read 151 to 165. Of the 11 jabs the catalog flagged, five read under 130 and got a launch multiplier on the plain swing only (JAB_TRIM; damage, reach, multi-hit counts, and the empowered jab of 'next attack hits harder' kits are untouched): Rose x0.75, Snowball x0.8, Tapey x0.8, Book x0.9, Barf Bag x0.95. Mid foe, centre stage, before -> after: Rose 114 -> 131, Snowball 118 -> 131, Tapey 118 -> 132, Book 124 -> 131, Barf Bag 128 -> 131; light foe 59 -> 80, 63 -> 79, 63 -> 80, 71 -> 79, 74 -> 78; at the ledge (mid foe) 89 -> 105, 93 -> 104, 94 -> 105, 99 -> 104, 105 -> 110. The old house probe (Pen at weight 90, launch KO at centre) agrees: 127 -> 145, 130 -> 144, 131 -> 145, 137 -> 144, 161 -> 167. Not trimmed because they already read 130 or more: Gelatin 149, David 160, Blueberry 141, Puffball 183 (a shot, no launch). Clover skipped as asked (142). Not done: outside the catalog's 31 fighters, jabs that read under 130 at centre are still there (Balloony 94, Profily 103, Saw 103, Blocky 108; 45 of the 109 are under 130 in all, 4 under 110): the owner decides whether those get the same trim. (3) FREEZES: the code cap is FREEZE_MAX 45, applyFreeze enforces it for every freeze and the counter did peak at 45 (Snowball 44), but a hit-stop holds the frozen fighter still and the freeze timer (and the 70-frame re-freeze gap, kept together) stood still with it, so the foe was held for 45 plus the hit-stop: 48 for a light hit (Gelatin's special and Freeze Mine, Ice Cube's special), 50 to 51 for a smash (Gelatin 51, Snowball 50, Ice Cube 50). Fix: the freeze timer and the gap now run on through the hit-stop frames (two lines where the hit-stop holds a fighter, in the main step). Frames frozen before -> after: Gelatin special / mine 48 -> 45, Gelatin smash 51 -> 45, Snowball smash 50 -> 44 (its own number: 44), Ice Cube special 48 -> 45, Ice Cube smash 50 -> 45; the re-freeze immunity after the freeze stays 70 frames (measured 70 before and after), freeze damage, the 40% threshold and the ice-breaks-on-a-hit rule are unchanged; a scan of all 109 fighters' jab, special, up, down, smash and finisher found no freeze above 45 now (Ice Cube's finisher block of ice, 30 frames, is a separate hold and was not touched). Per-fighter balance notes, the fighters touched: Black Hole (up throw launch down about 9%), Rose, Snowball, Tapey, Book, Barf Bag (plain jab launch trimmed), Gelatin, Snowball, Ice Cube (freezes now a true 45 frames or less, a small nerf of 3 to 6 frames). REPORTED, NOT CHANGED: (a) projectile start-up: ours fire on frame 2 to 4 on the jab-slot shots (Puffball's spit, Ruby's Gem Bolt, Pencil's van) against Smash's 8 to 41, median about 16; (b) dash attacks: the specials that dash set the attacker untouchable for the whole dash (10 to 18 frames), against none in Smash, and the 16-frame tell was only just added (g-dashtell); (c) roots last 33 to 89 frames (Rose's Rising Lash 33, Taco 40, Fries 53, Toothpaste 63 to 64, Lollipop 63 to 76, Tree's smash 75, Magnet's finisher 89, the longest); a rooted fighter can still attack and jump straight up. Checked: syntax, boot (FFA and Teams, no errors), the merged three-fighter free-for-alls (no errors), CRLF intact, 0 control bytes. Not verified: no Expert CPU win-rate re-run (the three changes are small and no fighter's jab moved more than 20% of its launch except Rose, Snowball and Tapey at 20 to 25%); the Smash numbers come from the owner's verified section of reports/smash-vs-ours.md.

- **2026-11-04, JAB NERF 2-4 (the owner: "def nerf all jabs to 2-4%. teardrop's should become 1.5 for balance"; branch `g-jabnerf`, NOT PUSHED):** Every fighter's plain jab now hits for 2% to 4% a hit. How: a jab above 4 was mapped linearly onto the band, new = 2 + (old - 4) / 4 to a tenth and never above 4 (so 5 -> 2.3, 8 -> 3, 10 -> 3.5, 12 -> 4: the order among the nerfed jabs is kept and Balloony's is still the strongest); a jab already within 2 to 4 stays; none was under 2; Teardrop's is 1.5 as the owner said. A multi-hit jab's per-HIT number is the one mapped (Toothpaste 2 x 5.7 -> 2 x 2.4, Barf Bag 2 x 5.2 -> 2 x 2.3). The empowered jab of a 'next attack hits much harder' kit keeps its ratio to the plain jab (its old number x new/old: a 5 jab that hit 14 empowered now hits 6.4 empowered; Teardrop's 9 is 4.5). Puffball's bop on a foe touching her front in the air was 13 and is 4 (her ground stings were 2 a hit and stay); Salt's Pepper echo was 4 and is 2 (it would otherwise have out-hit Salt's own 2.6). The three hidden fighters' jabs were 5 and are 2.3 (the default jab row, now 2.3). NOT CHANGED, on purpose: reach, start-up, knockback (the kb numbers), and the hit-stun, hit-grace and hit-freeze a jab gives. Those three are worked out from the damage, so a jab still stuns, chains and freezes exactly as it did (jabFeelK: they read the old damage); the up-tilt's damage is worked out from the jab's row too and reads the old number, so no up-tilt changed. One honest side effect: a launch is scaled by the foe's percent, which this hit's damage feeds, so from the same starting percent a jab launches a little slower (about 10% at 0%, fading as the percent climbs); the kb inputs are identical. Per-fighter before -> after per hit (98 fighters changed): 12 -> 4: Balloony; 11 -> 3.8: Profily; 10 -> 3.5: Ice Cube, Pencil, Saw, Yellow Face; 9 -> 3.3: Blocky, Coiny, Dora, Firey Jr., Lollipop, Naily, Rose, TV; 8.5 -> 3.1: Dough, Magnet, MeTag, Spongy; 8 -> 3: Baseball, Bomb, Bomby, Bonesaw, Book, Bracelety, Fern, Fries, Gaty, Pen, Pillow, Poppy, Snowball, Taco, Tennis Ball; 7.5 -> 2.9: Silver Spoon, Tapey; 7 -> 2.8: 8-Ball, Apple, Cherries, Donut, Eraser, Flower, Knife, Marker, Match, Money, Pickle, Pin, Rocky, Spikey, Taco (II), Tissues, Tree; 6.5 -> 2.6: Bow, Paintbrush, Salt, Soap; 6 -> 2.5: Balloon, Basketball, Bell, Box, Cake, Cheesy, Clock, Firey, Lightbulb, Loser, Marshmallow, Microphone, Nickel, Nickel (II), Paper, Pie, Remote, Roboty, Ruler, Sidewalky, Teddy Bear, Test Tube; 5.7 -> 2.4: Toothpaste; 5.5 -> 2.4: Black Hole, Cloudy; 5.2 -> 2.3: Barf Bag; 5 -> 2.3: Blueberry, Cammy, Candle, Clover, David, Fan, Golf Ball, Goo, Jack, Lifering, Lightning, Starfruit, Tea Kettle, Trophy, Yin-Yang; 3 -> 1.5: Teardrop. Unchanged (already 2 to 4): Bot, Bubble, Fanny, Gelatin, Grassy, Leafy, Liy, Needle, Puffball, Ruby, Woody (Puffball changed only in the air bop). THE NEUTRAL BUFF for the weakest nine (the weak-fighter report: they lose the neutral): the jab's whole reach x1.12 for Cammy, Lifering, Balloon, Starfruit, Tea Kettle, Box, Paper, Tissues and Apple (the swing's arc, 58 -> 65 px for six of them, Balloon 60 -> 67, Paper 64 -> 72, Apple 65 -> 73); reach only, no Teardrop. CLOVER (covered, not buffed): her jab 5 -> 2.3, the empowered one 14 -> 6.4; a scripted string (jab, up-tilt, down-tilt, jab, up-tilt on a still Pen) did 18.8% before and 13.4% after, the same hits landing and only the two jabs smaller (5 -> 2.3 each); her pinwheel and tilts are untouched. MEASURED (the scratchpad's `jabnerf/`; jsdom scenes against a Pen at 46 px, plain and empowered, all 109 fighters before and after; reports/jab-nerf-table.csv): hit-stun frames, kb inputs, hit count and hit timing identical for all 109 on both swings; no effective hit above 4 (the highest is Balloony 4 and Eraser 3.9 with his bonus). 20 CPU four-fighter free-for-alls (Expert, 3 stocks, items and smash balls off, the same 20 lineups and seeds): jab damage 10,390 -> 5,847 (38.4% -> 24.4% of all damage; 520 -> 292 a match), total damage 27,032 -> 23,959, average match 6,828 -> 6,774 frames (the median 6,960 -> 7,380; 3 matches hit the 9,000-frame cap after, 0 before, so the real average is longer), stocks lost 218 -> 212; one sample of 20, noisy. Checks: syntax 0 failed, boot clean (FFA and teams), merged_ffa3 clean, 0 control bytes, CRLF intact. NOT VERIFIED: no human played it; the hidden fighters were checked only by their rows (they are not in the roster until unlocked); the move text (MOVE_TEXT) was rewritten to the new numbers by script and read in a few cases, not on screen; the AI still plans with its old idea of its own jab reach (brainReach), so the buffed nine approach as before; reports/move-catalog.csv is a stale generated file and was not regenerated.

CPU: the same run code; its brains read st.run where they predict a walk (fx8Ahead), the netcode sends mvB/capB x st (netPredOut), the CTF routes check each move with the fighter's own st. | 2026-11-09 | ONLINE LAG (branch g-lag, on ii-dlc 672b0e9; not pushed; NO relay: nothing here connected to, probed or redeployed the live relay or any server -- every measurement is two jsdom pages in one node process) | The owner (2026-11-09): "lag spikes high with 3+ players on multiplayer"; later: free-for-all, they were a GUEST, the spikes come every few seconds. MEASURED OFFLINE (scripts/net-lag-measure.mjs, net-lag-guest.mjs: a host page steps a busy CPU free-for-all with items on and encodes a snapshot every frame as broadcastState does; a guest page parses, applies, glides, predicts and draws it; 3000-7200 frames): the host's snapshot work is small and grows in a straight line with the fighters -- encode mean/p95/max 0.05/0.09/0.8 ms at 2 players, 0.08/0.14/0.7 at 4, 0.26/0.38/4.7 at 8 (step() itself 0.3 / 0.55 / 1.5 ms); the guest's apply+glide+prediction 0.33 / 0.6 / 1.26 ms a frame (prediction 0.01 ms); no per-pair loop anywhere in the net code; guest and host agree (positions within 1 px, percents, stocks, items, shots, platforms: 0 mismatches in every run). So the lag is not the net code's CPU: it is BYTES on the wire and what fattens one snapshot. Before: 59 KB/s at 2 players, 70 at 3, 93 at 4 (60 snapshots a second of 0.98 / 1.16 / 1.56 KB; the relay sends each to every guest, so 3 guests = 280 KB/s out of it), 154 KB/s with 8 fighters; TOP SOURCES: (1) the fighters, two thirds of every snapshot, and a third of THAT was slow fields sent 60 times a second -- name, colour, kit, KO cap, team (about 95 bytes a fighter) and a guest's eleven prediction numbers pr.k (about 110 bytes a free guest); (2) YOYLE NEEDLE re-sent its WHOLE geometry in every snapshot (2991 of 3000) because the moving ledges' places were in the geometry's key: 2.27 KB a snapshot, 136 KB/s at 4 players; (3) particle bursts: a hit's 48 rows with the colour string written on each were 1.7 KB of a 3.3 KB snapshot (the biggest single-frame spike on a flat stage); (4) the geometry repeat every 3 s: +0.6 KB on Goiky, +7 KB on a Huge big-FFA map (8.9 KB snapshot) -- the one PERIODIC fattening in the protocol; (5) on the guest, garbage collection from the per-snapshot objects: in node every 1.5 s a 4-10 ms pause lands inside applySnapshot (the only spiky part of the guest's frame; a browser's young-generation pauses are smaller but the mechanism is the same). FIXED: a slow field now goes when it changes, through the first 2 s of a match, with the geometry, and once a second regardless (NET_STAT, netStatDue); the guest keeps the last it saw (applySnapshot) and carries what a skipped snapshot had (netSnapshotArrived); false `dead` / `onground` ride as nothing; the geometry's key no longer holds the platforms' places, and a platform that has moved since the geometry went rides as an `mv` row (index, x, y; the guest puts the rest back where the geometry had them each snapshot -- NET_VIEW.geoBase); particle rows carry a colour index into a per-snapshot table `pc` (resolved by name when an older snapshot's rows are carried into a newer one), and the cap is 32 rows (was 48); the geometry repeat is every 8 s (was 3). AFTER, same seeds: 46 KB/s at 2 players (0.77 KB), 55 at 3 (0.92), 67 at 4 (1.11 KB; p95 1.55, max 2.5 KB, was 2.04 / 3.6), 73 on Canyon Huge (max 7.3 KB, was 8.9), 72 on Yoyle Needle (was 136; geometry 7 times in 50 s, was 2991), 129 with 8 fighters (was 154): -22% to -47%; encode and guest apply unchanged within noise (0.095 / 0.165 / 4.8 ms encode at 4; guest 0.64 ms). Wire: new fields only (mv, pc, the absence of fields): a guest on this build reads an old host's snapshot as before; an old guest on a new host would show nameless fighters (both ends run the same build; the start message refuses another build). Single-player and local play run none of this (serializeState and applySnapshot are the host's and the guest's alone). Also tried: a jittered wire (net-pair, 60 ms +-40 ms) for periodic prediction corrections on the guest's own fighter -- 7 in a minute, not periodic; the ack window is not it. NOT TESTABLE OFFLINE: the relay's throughput and its fan-out to 3 guests, the host's upload, wifi jitter, a browser's own GC and draw time; a real room on this build is the next check. Checks: syncheck 0 failed; bootcheck ok (ffa/teams bad positions 0, errors none; guards control bytes 0, bare LF 0, hidden names none; kit guard ok); guest-vs-host state equality 0 mismatches in 9 runs; no errors in any run. No changelog entry. |

WHERE THE DESIGN'S NUMBERS WERE WRONG AND WHAT WAS DONE: (a) 'at' on Star Rain and Card Spray, and 'grow' on the three bursts, do not set the startup (the stars fall from 620 px up at a start speed; a burst waits the smash press, then CIRCLE_WINDUP 8, then the ring): the stars got rider vy 16 (a faster fall; the shadow tell is unchanged), the bursts wind 4 and frames 8 (grow left alone), which lands the same targets; (b) the design's kill-power table was a probe artifact: ko.mjs fired the move again in the same setup, the second cast met the move's own cooldown and read as 'no KO', so every plant, lunge and beam showed 133% or 175%. | 2026-11-10 | MOON v4 stuck-in-rock fix (branch g-moonfix, on ii-dlc b84c3957; not pushed; no relay; the HIDDEN stage Moon Caves v4 only) | The owner (with a picture): Pen, right after being launched, stuck in the wall on Moon Caves v4, tilted, still drifting at vx about -4.8 with no stun left, at a corner where two rock faces meet. ROOT CAUSES (two, both found by launching fighters on the moons in a jsdom harness and measuring the body's overlap with the rock pieces in its own chart): (1) WEDGE: the fighter step pushes a body out of each solid piece in turn along that piece's shortest axis, once, and never looks again; in a gap narrower than the body (a 42 px slot against the 48 px body, a piece on each side) the left piece pushes it right 6 and the right piece pushes it back left 6, so it ends every frame 6 px in one piece and stays until gravity slides it out (13 frames in the repro, for ever under a steady drift). (2) TUNNELLING: a launch moves a body 30-60 px a frame and the rock is 16-21 px thin in places, so the push-out sees it already through (or half into a thick piece): 27-48 px deep for 20 frames, and 3 of the trials never got out in 150 frames. FIX (index.html only, all guarded by MCAVE.v === 4, a stage check that is false everywhere else): mc4Sweep (the step's move, only past 8 px a frame: the move is cut at the first solid piece in its way, one axis at a time, ending 0.02 px into the face so the step's own push-out still sets the wall side, bonk, landing and drops the speed); mc4Unstick (the end of a fighter's frame, in its chart: if the body still overlaps a solid piece by more than half a pixel, the shortest single shift out, tie against its speed, 96 px at most; and if that fails for more than 6 frames in a row, the nearest free place by rings, the last place it was clear of rock preferred, speed dropped). Damage, stun and launch are never touched; the roster, other stages and the live Boss Rush run none of it. BEFORE/AFTER (launch test: one fighter on 4 of the 4v4 moons' free spots within about 110 px of rock, 7 fighters from Puffball to Bell and Pen, random direction, speed 6-60, stun 20-70, 150 frames, everyone else standing still; 'embedded' = centre inside rock for 6+ frames in a row; moons 4-01, 6-01, 8-01 and 1, 2, 11, 13, 15 of the same size, 300 trials each = 2,400): ii-dlc 8 embedded (9 counting a shallow 4 px overlap), 3 of them still in the rock at frame 150 (longest 150 frames); this branch 0 (and 0 shallow). With only the unstick and fallback and no sweep (first version, moons 4, 6, 8) it was 3 of 900, none longer than 6 frames. Launches from anywhere (not near rock) on 3 moons, 1,680 trials, ii-dlc: 1 embedded; this branch not re-run. Three CPU 4v4 matches of 4,500 frames (moons 4, 6, 8) on ii-dlc showed none. The fallback was exercised by placing a fighter inside thick rock 12 times: 12 freed (8 at once by the shift, 4 by the nearest-free-place fallback on the 7th frame), damage unchanged. | 2026-11-11 | OC: online sync (branch g-oc-net, on ii-dlc 568e415c; not pushed; no relay touched; HIDDEN: OC_OPEN off, and OC_PUBLIC_TYPES is still ['zoner'] so only the Zoner is accepted over the wire until the owner opens the others) | An OC now plays the same for host and guest. The relay keeps only 24 characters of a hello, so an OC hello says 'OC' and the build (the existing ocWireEncode code) rides a lobby input message the relay already routes to the host (NET.sendOc / ocIn, capped 300 characters, 64 senders). At the start the host checks every build with ocNetBuild (ocWireDecode > ocHostClean > ocCheckPicks: over-budget picks, an unknown move or type, a bad or long name become the type's default build, name 'OC'; no build received: the default OC), makes the names unique, and sends start.oc (canonical codes); the host and every guest rebuild the seat from that code (beginMatch > window.__netOC > buildFighters). Free-for-all and Teams only (a Capture the Flag or boss room seats an OC as Firey). Each snapshot carries the code as a slow field (NET_STAT, with name, colour, kit); a guest rebuilds f.oc from it (ocSnapBuild, cached), so look, Final Smash and reflector draw as on the host, and f.name is always the checked name, never raw text. The skipped-snapshot merge (netSnapshotArrived) now carries the code too (it was the one lag path that lost it: found by the first run). OC mines, shots, beams and floor pieces are ordinary projectiles/beams and already rode the snapshot; the finishers' records ride FINX_NET (no new fields needed). The OC board tiles are no longer locked in a room and the lobby no longer drops a picked OC. Tests (offline, fake sockets, host/guest pairs with AI-driven OCs, latency 30 jitter 10): 8 archetype pairs (each type as host and guest) x FFA/Teams x 2 stages x 3000 frames, with all four types enabled in the test copy only: 0 errors, builds and names identical on both sides in every run, 0 build mismatches. Tampered builds (two kill hits off-type, unknown move, 5000-character name with script, short script name, unknown type): identical, safe result on both sides (default build; name 'OC' or the clean name). Dropped snapshots (60 and 20 frames): builds and final stocks agree. Honest caveats: a few sampled frames per run show a position gap over 120 px (up to about 1000 px) or a one-sample stock difference, which line up with KOs and respawns (the guest glides); not traced event by event. Projectile counts match in about 94% to 100% of samples (they differ by one shot for a frame while a snapshot is in flight). The 'needle' Teams runs repeat the goiky Teams numbers exactly, so that stage id probably fell back in Teams; Needle FFA ran on its own. A guest whose build arrives after the host presses Start plays the default OC. No-op for non-OC play: the roster rows and 11 seeded matches (10 FFA, 1 Teams, 700 frames) are identical to ii-dlc; bootcheck clean. |

- **MOON CAVES v4: CPU stuck spots (S4) (2026-11-11, Moon Caves v4; branch `g-moon-s4b` from ii-dlc 37e7d825, NOT PUSHED; HIDDEN stage, `MC_V4_OPEN` false; geometry, plans and the frozen table untouched)** -- V9's S4 harness (its t4-match.mjs, itemRate 2, seed 7+n, 180 s) reproduced the report on current ii-dlc: 6 stuck windows at 4 a side on 4-05 (V9: 4), 24 at 10 a side on 10-03. CAUSE (logged per window with the CPU's chart node, goal, route hop and `mcStill`): not fighting in place (no foe within 250 px in most windows). A CPU with a cache-item goal on a plank in its own room (node 17 or 15, the 3 and 9 o'clock homes) used the generic climb (`navUp` via `mc4Near`), which picks the nearest reachable step -- a lift's step in the room next door; it walked out, the graph route (`mc4Route`) walked it back in, and the 40 px cost test and the stand-still test (`mcStill`, speed under 0.6 px a frame) never saw it, so only the 300-frame no-progress timer ended it. FIX (CPU routing only, `mc4Cpu`): the goal is also given up when the CPU stays inside a 60 px box for 150 frames (`MC4G.box`, `MC4G.pace`). It does NOT fix why the climb prefers the wrong step (that is `navUp`, shared by every stage; not touched). MEASURED, stuck windows (300 frames under 80 px) before to after: 4 a side 4-05 6/6 to 0/0 (two seeds), moon 2 9/7 to 1/1, moon 9 13/15 to 8/16 (NOT fixed: a different, longer stall, up to 1100 frames still); 10 a side 10-03 24/30 to 0/2, moon 7 0/0 to 0/0. S4 is therefore NOT met on every moon: moon 9 (4 a side) remains, and 10-03 seed+100 still has 2 windows (longest 808 frames). The 150-frame box is a give-up rule, not a change to the check; the check was not changed. No-op: 3 CPU FFAs byte-identical to the unmodified build; the 40-match batch cannot show it (the unmodified build differs from itself run to run), the edit sits behind `MCAVE.on && v === 4`; syncheck failed 0, bootcheck clean. No browser. |
